text: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song. His foundation stands on the holy mountains;

versions.text: Of the sons of Korah. A psalm. A song. He has founded his city on the holy mountains;
versions.explanation: The Hebrew is a noun clause, "his foundation is on the holy mountains," with no explicit object "his city." The added noun narrows the sense; a closer rendering keeps the poetry and avoids interpretive expansion, while still reading smoothly aloud.

text: the LORD loves the gates of Zion more than all the dwellings of Jacob.
Glorious things are said of you, city of God. Selah
"I will record Rahab and Babylon among those who know me — see, Philistia too, and Tyre, along with Cush: this one was born there."
And of Zion it will be said, "This one and that one were born in her," and the Most High himself will establish her.
The LORD will write in the register of the peoples: "This one was born there." Selah
Singers and dancers alike: "All my springs are in you."

versions.text: And as they sing and dance they will say, "All my springs are in you."
versions.explanation: The Hebrew has no verb of speaking; "they will say" is supplied. The nouns "singers" and "dancers/pipers" are participial nouns, and a tighter rendering preserves the abrupt, exclamatory close of the psalm while remaining easy to read aloud.
